reports.title: Endurance training attenuates acute exercise-induced monocyte transcriptomic responses in adolescents: sex-specific molecular adaptations
reports.authors: Plaza-Florido A; Haddad F; Cooper DM; Radom-Aizik S
reports.version_date: published 2026 (J Appl Physiol 141:873-887); first published online 2026-08-03; submitted 2026-03-24, revised 2026-07-06, accepted 2026-07-27
source_locator: p.873 header: 'First published August 3, 2026; doi:10.1152/japplphysiol.00282.2026'; p.875 footer: 'Submitted 24 March 2026 / Revised 6 July 2026 / Accepted 27 July 2026'
reports.reviewer_notes: provisional FT code: FT03_POPULATION_NOT_ELIGIBLE. Cohort is 12 males + 9 females, 13-17 yr (abstract p.873; Table 1 age 15.2+/-1.3 y males, 15.2+/-1.5 y females; p.876 Results '15 +/- 1 yr'), i.e. all participants under 18 y with no adult (>=18 y) stratum present at all (not a mixed-age cohort with a separable adult layer -- there is no adult layer to separate). Per v3 design contract 2.3 ('Children and adolescents (<18 y) are excluded') and fulltext_exclusion_codes.json FT03 definition/example ('Adolescent-only cohort (for example 13-17 y)'), this report fails population eligibility outright; it is not an 'awaiting classification' case because age is explicitly and precisely reported (contract: unreported age remains awaiting classification, not FT03 -- age IS reported here). The exercise exposure (identifiable single acute bout: 10x2-min cycling at 70% max work rate) and immune link (monocyte transcriptome, monocyte counts) would otherwise plausibly satisfy Core A criteria (post-cessation sample, pre-exercise baseline, immune-cell omics), so population is the sole/first-established failure reason in the FT01-FT08 hierarchy -- confirmed FT03 is reached only after checking FT01/FT02 do not apply (this is an original peer-reviewed human research article, not excluded by FT01/FT02). primary_fulltext_exclusion_reason and consensus_screening_decision are left null per manual section 'Report, cohort and sample denominators' item 3/'double extraction' section (primary_fulltext_exclusion_reason is null unless consensus_screening_decision=EXCLUDE_FT, which is reserved for reconciliation by D); this provisional code is my (reviewer-C stand-in) individual full-text disposition only. Locator for age: p.873 Abstract 'Twelve males and nine females (13-17 yr) completed an acute exercise protocol'; p.876 Table 1 and Results 'Twelve males and nine females (15 +/- 1 yr)'.
reports.author_stated_use: p.887 Conclusions: 'The functional implications of these transcriptional changes and their relevance to long-term cardiovascular health remain to be determined.' p.883 Discussion: 'the identified pathways should primarily be interpreted as mechanistic and hypothesis-generating insights into exercise-induced immune regulation during adolescence, rather than direct biomarkers of clinical benefit.' No diagnostic, prognostic, infection-risk, or return-to-training use is proposed; framing is mechanistic/exploratory CVD-risk-pathway discovery in a pediatric population.
author_window_interpretation_locator: Full-text search of the complete main text (Abstract through Acknowledgments/Grants, p.873-887) found zero occurrences of 'open window', 'immunosuppress*', 'susceptib*', or 'redistribut*'; the paper's entire interpretive frame is cardiovascular-disease/atherogenesis pathway biology and trained-innate-immunity, e.g. p.887 Conclusions: 'Endurance training attenuates the monocyte transcriptomic response to acute exercise in adolescents...providing insight into how exercise training influences monocyte behavior during a critical developmental period.'

report_cohort_links.report_specific_population: All 21 enrolled adolescents (12 M, 9 F) had valid monocyte transcriptome data at up to 4 timepoints (p.875 'Bioinformatic Analysis': 'All participants (21 adolescents) had valid monocyte transcriptome data at four time points, except for one female participant who had a missing blood sample post-acute exercise session conducted after the training period'). For the pre-training acute-exercise differential-expression analysis, 1 male was excluded as a PCA outlier at both his pre-training timepoints, giving an analytic n of 11 males + 9 females (p.877 Fig. 3 legend). For the post-training acute-exercise differential-expression analysis, the female with the missing post-training post-exercise sample was excluded, giving an analytic n of 12 males + 8 females (p.877 Fig. 3 legend).

precision_validation.evidence_notes: Marker family = immune_cell_transcriptome (monocyte whole-transcriptome RNA-seq). Reported analytical-reliability indicators: monocyte isolation purity mean 90.8% (range 79-97%) by CD14-FITC flow cytometry; RNA integrity number (RIN) 6.7-10 (avg 9.59) by Agilent Bioanalyzer prior to library prep; standardized pipeline (fastQC v0.11.9, trimmomatic v0.39, HiSat2 v2.2.1 to GRCh38, SAMtools v1.3, featureCounts v2.0.1/v1.5.0-p3); PCA-based outlier detection and exclusion (1 male outlier at 2 timepoints). No technical-replicate concordance, inter-assay CV, or cross-platform reliability (e.g. RNA-seq vs. qPCR confirmation) is reported for this cohort's samples -- those pieces of analytical reliability remain NR.

source_locator: p.874 'Study Design', Fig. 1; p.875 'Blood Sampling and Analysis'
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Samples fall in two time_bin categories: pre_exercise_baseline (30 min after catheter placement, before exercise onset) and 0_to_lt30min (immediately post-exercise), both within_window per within_organising_window; collected at 4 timepoints total (pre-/post-training x pre-/post-acute-exercise). No 30min-3h, 3h-24h, 24h-72h-inclusive, or >72h (outside_window_recovery) post-exercise samples were collected for this acute-exercise challenge -- only the single immediate post-exercise timepoint documents the acute response; no recovery trajectory beyond the immediate point is established for this exposure (consistent with the single-timepoint response-measurement allowance in contract 2.1, which explicitly cannot establish a recovery trajectory).

Cell-lineage specificity to monocytes is well supported procedurally (negative immunomagnetic depletion of T/NK/B/dendritic/basophil lineages, CD14-FITC purity 79-97%, mean 90.8%). However, whether the observed exercise-induced transcriptomic signal reflects intrinsic transcriptional reprogramming within monocytes versus a shift in the relative proportions of monocyte subsets (classical/intermediate/nonclassical) mobilized into circulation is explicitly NOT resolved by the authors: 'Because immunophenotypic characterization of monocyte subsets was not performed, we cannot distinguish whether the observed transcriptomic responses to acute exercise reflect intrinsic transcriptional remodeling within monocytes, shifts in monocyte subset distribution, or a combination of both mechanisms' (p.883 Discussion). This is recorded as not_demonstrated for the specificity-of-mechanism question, while lineage-purity reporting itself is evidence_present (see notes); the report does not separately resolve these two aspects, so the more conservative state is recorded for this domain.

precision_validation.response_evidence: Within-subject pre/post change observed and training-attenuated; no variance/reproducibility quantification.
precision_validation.individualization: Observed individual-level (within-subject) change across repeated timepoints; no ICC/CV/SEM/reference-change-value or responder definition reported.
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Within-subject repeated-measures design (same participants sampled before/after acute exercise and before/after the 8-wk training intervention) demonstrates that individual-level transcriptomic change was observed and that training attenuated the within-person response magnitude (e.g. individual-level log2FC for IL-10 expression: males 1.15 pre-training vs. 0.72 post-training; females 1.17 pre-training vs. 1.12 post-training, p.883). No individual-level noise/reproducibility estimate (ICC, CV, SEM, reference change value), no responder-vs-non-responder definition, and no individualized threshold/model validation are reported. Per manual guidance this is recorded as: individual-level change observed; natural variability/measurement error not quantified -- not termed an individualized marker.

precision_validation.functional_evidence: No direct in vitro/ex vivo/in vivo functional assay performed; pathway-enrichment/database annotation only (not functional evidence per manual rule).
source_locator: p.879-881 'Molecular pathways'; p.883 Discussion; p.887 Conclusions
precision_validation.evidence_notes: No direct functional immune assay (e.g. stimulated cytokine secretion, phagocytosis, killing, proliferation) was performed in this report. IPA canonical-pathway analysis (Z-score, FDR<0.1), DAVID/KEGG enrichment (EASE score<0.1), and PHENOPEDIA gene-disease-association overlap are bioinformatic annotation/enrichment analyses on differentially expressed transcripts, not measured immune function or clinical outcomes (per manual: GO/pathway/database outputs are annotations or hypotheses, not measured immune function). No symptom, infection, or other clinical follow-up was conducted; this is a mechanistic discovery study in healthy adolescents with no infection/illness endpoint. Authors explicitly state: 'identified pathways should primarily be interpreted as mechanistic and hypothesis-generating insights...rather than direct biomarkers of clinical benefit' (p.883) and 'functional implications of these transcriptional changes and their relevance to long-term cardiovascular health remain to be determined' (p.887 Conclusions).

precision_validation.replication: No independent cohort/site replication; qualitative concordance noted with the same laboratory's prior young-adult-male studies (refs 1, 5), not a formal external validation.
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Single-cohort, single-site, within-cohort analysis; no independent cohort replication, no participant-level holdout, and no resampling-based internal validation reported for the differential-expression or pathway findings (standard DE statistics with FDR correction, not a predictive model requiring a train/validation split). No proposed clinical/field use was tested; the report frames candidates as hypothesis-generating only (p.883, p.887). Comparison to the authors' prior work in young adult males (refs 1, 5) is a cross-study qualitative concordance check (same lab, different age group/cohort, not a formal independent validation of this adolescent cohort's findings).

precision_validation.field_feasibility: Demonstrated feasible as a supervised laboratory research protocol in healthy adolescents (low attrition: 1/21 missing sample, 1/21 analytic outlier); not evaluated as a field/point-of-care assay.
source_locator: p.874 'Study Design'; p.875 'Blood Sampling and Analysis', 'Monocyte Isolation', 'Bioinformatic Analysis'
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Feasibility is demonstrated for a laboratory-research pediatric protocol: venous catheterization, acute exercise challenge, and monocyte isolation/RNA-seq were successfully completed in 21 adolescents (12 M, 9 F) across 4 timepoints with written parental consent and child assent, with only 1 missing sample (post-training post-exercise, 1 female) and 1 PCA-based analytic exclusion (1 male outlier) reported -- i.e. low attrition/exclusion in a demanding repeated-sampling pediatric design. This is lab-based, multi-step feasibility (indwelling catheter, density-gradient PBMC isolation, immunomagnetic monocyte selection, poly(A)-selected RNA-seq library prep, NovaSeq sequencing at ~30M reads/sample) -- not a field-deployable or point-of-care assay; no cost, turnaround-time, or point-of-care feasibility data are reported.
